name: Daohua
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Acuo, Yeshes Vodgsal 2004. Daohua Yanjiu [A study of Daohua], Beijing: Ethnic Publishing House (346pp long grammar, per Glottolog); print-only Chinese monograph, not online

new_statements.quote: 倒话共有四个声调调类。其具体调类调值为（按倒话中汉语词的阴阳上去排列）：1调：高平降554；2调：中平降332；3调：高降51；4调：中降升324。为了简明起见，在文中以各调调号标调，不标调值。[...] 说明：1）倒话的声调又可以分为高、低（或高、中）两组，A、C两调可称为高调，B、D两调可称为低（中）调。这样分组之后还可以发现每组内部各有长短调的不同：A、D两调即又表现为长调，B、C两调又表现为短调。倒话元音长短可以视为不同声调的伴随特征。2）倒话里除四个声调外，还有轻声现象，主要是各种语法标志中的一些音节，轻声在本书中不标调；在自然语流中，还有变调现象。
new_statements.translation: Daohua has four tone categories. Their values (ordered by the yinping/yangping/shang/qu of the Chinese-derived words in Daohua) are: tone 1 high level-falling 554; tone 2 mid level-falling 332; tone 3 high falling 51; tone 4 mid falling-rising 324. For simplicity, tones are marked in the text by category number, not by value. [...] Notes: 1) The Daohua tones can further be grouped into high and low (or high and mid): A and C may be called high tones, B and D low (mid) tones. Within each group there is also a long/short difference: A and D are long tones, B and C short tones; vowel length in Daohua can be regarded as a concomitant feature of the tones. 2) Besides the four tones, Daohua also has 'light tone' (toneless/neutral) syllables, mainly certain syllables of grammatical markers; light tone is not marked in this book. In natural connected speech there is also tone sandhi.
new_statements.citation: 意西微萨·阿错 (Yeshes Vodgsal Atshogs). 2004. 倒话研究 [A study of Daohua]. 中国新发现语言研究丛书. 北京: 民族出版社.
new_statements.locator: 第一章 第二节 二、语音系统概述 (三) 声调, book pp.15-16 (PDF pp.25-26); cf. p.249 (PDF p.259)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Daohua is described as a syllable-tone language with four lexical tones (554, 332, 51, 324) on full syllables (the Chinese-derived lexicon keeps regular correspondences with the four Mandarin tone categories), a high/low register grouping with vowel length as a by-product of tone, toneless ('轻声') grammatical-marker syllables, and tone sandhi in connected speech; the grammar makes no statement about word stress or a stress position for Daohua (its 重音/'tone-stress' analysis, pp.214, 242-248, is of Wutun, and p.249 notes that both of Daohua's source languages have similar tone systems).
new_statements.exceptions: Grammatical-marker syllables are toneless (轻声, unmarked in the book); tone sandhi occurs in connected speech (not described in detail in this section); /ɛ/ and /uɛ/ have allophones conditioned by tone 4 (去声) vs. the other tones (pp.14-15).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (citation-form) syllable tones; instrumental F0 and duration averages per tone from one female speaker (b.1974, 河口镇城厢村), recorded 2000, analysed 2001 at Nankai (pp.16-18). Toneless syllables are affixal/grammatical markers, i.e. a word-level full-syllable vs. reduced-syllable asymmetry, but no stress rule is formulated.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes 雅江倒话 (Yajiang Daohua, also called 河口语 'Hekou speech'), spoken in 河口镇, 八角楼乡, 呷拉乡 of Yajiang (Nyagchukha) County, Garze, Sichuan — exactly Glottolog daoh1239 (no ISO code). Instrumental tone data from one speaker of 河口镇城厢村. The book's stress ('声调重音') analysis on pp.214-248 is of Wutun (wutu1241), not Daohua, and must not be attributed to daoh1239.
